name: ponytail
description: Makes your AI agent think like the laziest senior dev in the room. The best code is the code you never wrote.
one_liner: A skill that makes your AI coding assistant write the smallest correct amount of code instead of the biggest impressive-looking amount — reusing what's already in your codebase before adding anything new.
buyer: An engineering lead at a startup who's watched their AI coding bill and codebase size balloon and wants both back under control.
business_use_cases: A startup CTO installs it fleet-wide to cut AI coding token spend and reduce the backlog of 'AI-generated cruft' their senior devs have to clean up.
A fractional CTO consultancy offers a paid 'AI coding hygiene audit' that installs and tunes this skill across a client's repos.
An engineering training company builds a workshop around the before/after examples to teach 'lean AI-assisted coding' as a billable course.

money_ideas.idea: Sell a one-time 'AI coding cost audit' that benchmarks a client's current token/line-of-code spend against a Ponytail-equipped baseline.
Offer ongoing fractional-CTO retainers that include maintaining this and similar coding-discipline skills across a client's agents.

steal_this: This is a dev-productivity tool, not a product in itself — the honest weekend project is running its own benchmark against your team's current AI setup and pitching the savings number to your manager, not trying to sell the skill itself.
